goal: Determine a risk-based, falsifiable expansion of Invoke Design coverage: when UX planning should apply beyond explicit UI requests, how architecture design should be strengthened, which additional design blind spots need owned companions or gates, and what minimal changes belong in the current lifecycle-progress package.
context: The current Invoke Design contract requires six views and offers candidate architecture and UX-plan companions, but selection remains broad and evidence of completion is mostly authored structure. Inventory evidence shows defects involving operator trust, learning and navigation projections, authority and abuse, runtime enforcement, state divergence, persistence, accessibility, performance, claim bounds, and authored-versus-ready status. Research must inspect the live Invoke contracts and a bounded sample of recent Design packages, compare them with current primary or official human-centered-design, accessibility, architecture, security, reliability, and operations sources, and produce a trigger matrix that avoids both under-design and universal template bloat. The accepted result may add a private research finding and bounded change requests to ops/development/2026-07-24-invoke-lifecycle-progress-update; it does not authorize canonical Arcanum mutation, template promotion, implementation, publication, commit, or push.
anti_bias_global: expand Design coverage only where a falsifiable risk trigger and earliest-detection benefit justify the added work; prefer strengthening an owned companion over inventing a new family

agents.angle: Human-outcome and cognitive-risk mapping over local operator, approval, learning, explanation, recovery, content, mobile, and accessibility evidence plus primary or official human-centered-design and accessibility sources. Tversky predicts that van Lamsweerde's structural completeness can pass while human comprehension and recovery still fail, while van Lamsweerde predicts that Tversky may duplicate workflow and state concerns already owned by architecture. Tversky predicts that Ashby's invisible-risk framing may omit discoverability and user-controlled recovery, while Ashby predicts that Tversky may over-index visible interactions and miss systemic failure modes. Tversky predicts that Alexander's local package sample may normalize historical under-selection, while Alexander predicts that Tversky's normative corpus may trigger UX plans without demonstrated local risk.
agents.initial_prompt: Perform read-only research on when Invoke should select a UX-plan companion beyond requests explicitly labeled UI or UX. Inspect the live Invoke Design and UX-plan contracts, the current lifecycle-progress package, the supplied Inventory packet, and representative local evidence for operator, approval, learning, explanation, recovery, evidence, content, responsive, and accessibility surfaces. Compare against current primary or official sources such as ISO human-centred-design guidance where accessible, W3C WCAG and WAI guidance, and other directly owned standards. Derive candidate trigger signals, required UX-plan sections, negative or not-applicable cases, and falsifiable acceptance evidence. Distinguish human experience from visual styling and do not assume every backend change needs a UX plan. Cite repository paths and direct external links with dates. Do not edit files. Return concise evidence-backed prose suitable for verbatim inclusion under an Agent heading in research.md.

agents.angle: Scenario-based architecture analysis over the six current views, source contracts, quality attributes, authority, runtime enforcement, state, persistence, concurrency, integration, and deployment using local architecture failures plus primary or official architecture sources. Tversky predicts that van Lamsweerde's structural completeness can pass while human comprehension and recovery still fail, while van Lamsweerde predicts that Tversky may duplicate workflow and state concerns already owned by architecture. van Lamsweerde predicts that Ashby may split operational qualities into new companions even when quality-attribute scenarios belong in one architecture artifact, while Ashby predicts that van Lamsweerde's view model may document structure without proving runtime resilience. van Lamsweerde predicts that Alexander's historical sample may mistake common omission for minimal sufficiency, while Alexander predicts that van Lamsweerde's standards-derived coverage may create non-falsifiable document completeness.
agents.initial_prompt: Perform read-only research on how Invoke architecture design should improve beyond its six-view baseline. Inspect the live Invoke Design and architecture template contracts, the current lifecycle-progress Design, the supplied Inventory packet, and representative local architecture findings. Compare against primary or official architecture sources, including ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 material where accessible, SEI quality-attribute scenario and architecture-evaluation material, and official sources for any other adopted method. Test coverage for runtime enforcement, authority and trust boundaries, state and event semantics, persistence and concurrency, failure and compensation, integration and versioning, deployment and operability, data lifecycle, security and abuse, and architecture decisions with trade-offs. Produce a minimal core plus risk-triggered extensions, explicit counterexamples to the current template, and validator-friendly evidence. Do not turn every topic into a mandatory section without a trigger. Cite repository paths and direct external links with dates. Do not edit files. Return concise evidence-backed prose suitable for verbatim inclusion under an Agent heading in research.md.

agents.angle: Failure-first systems analysis over security, privacy, safety, resilience, observability, performance, capacity, data lifecycle, migration, rollback, support, and operational ownership using local incident-shaped evidence plus primary or official assurance and operations sources. Tversky predicts that Ashby's invisible-risk framing may omit discoverability and user-controlled recovery, while Ashby predicts that Tversky may over-index visible interactions and miss systemic failure modes. van Lamsweerde predicts that Ashby may split operational qualities into new companions even when quality-attribute scenarios belong in one architecture artifact, while Ashby predicts that van Lamsweerde's view model may document structure without proving runtime resilience. Ashby predicts that Alexander's frequency sample will underweight rare catastrophic failures, while Alexander predicts that Ashby's tail-risk lens may impose heavyweight gates on low-risk changes.
agents.initial_prompt: Perform read-only failure-first research into design blind spots not fully named by the current Invoke Design, architecture, or UX-plan contracts. Inspect the current lifecycle-progress package, the supplied Inventory packet, and representative local evidence. Use current primary or official sources where relevant, such as NIST security, privacy, and secure-development frameworks, OWASP-owned threat-model guidance, Google SRE or equivalent first-party reliability material, OpenTelemetry specifications, and official migration or compatibility guidance. Determine which risks belong inside architecture or UX, which warrant an optional owned companion, and which should remain downstream plan or validation concerns. Require concrete trigger signals, owner boundaries, earliest detection, negative fixtures, and not-applicable rationale. Cover security and abuse, privacy and data lifecycle, reliability and recovery, observability and operability, performance and capacity, migration and rollout, and support or incident response without claiming all are universally required. Cite repository paths and direct external links with dates. Do not edit files. Return concise evidence-backed prose suitable for verbatim inclusion under an Agent heading in research.md.

Tversky predicts that Alexander's local package sample may normalize historical under-selection, while Alexander predicts that Tversky's normative corpus may trigger UX plans without demonstrated local risk. van Lamsweerde predicts that Alexander's historical sample may mistake common omission for minimal sufficiency, while Alexander predicts that van Lamsweerde's standards-derived coverage may create non-falsifiable document completeness. agents.initial_prompt: Perform a read-only empirical audit of recent Invoke Design artifacts. Declare a bounded sample across UI or operator workflows, formal or evidence systems, infrastructure or lifecycle changes, integrations, and simple low-risk work. For each, record which companions were selected, which later defect or blocker was discoverable at design time, whether a proposed new section would have detected it, and the cost or false-positive risk of requiring that section. Inspect the live Design, architecture, UX-plan, research, implementation-layering, work-pack, Distill, and decision-gate boundaries so the result does not create duplicate owners. Produce a compact coverage matrix, denominator limits, examples where UX or architecture is not warranted, and evidence for required versus recommended triggers. Do not browse broadly unless needed to verify an official local template precedent. Cite exact repository paths. Do not edit files. Return concise evidence-backed prose suitable for verbatim inclusion under an Agent heading in research.md.

groups.anti_bias: reconcile blind-spot coverage into the smallest triggerable model and kill additions without a defect witness, owner, or validator

agents.angle: Bounded-rationality synthesis that converts normative coverage, failure analysis, and observed local omissions into proportional Design decisions rather than universal document expansion.
agents.initial_prompt: Synthesize the four explorer returns and the Strategy Inventory Packet. Produce: a taxonomy of design risks and current owners; a required, recommended, and not-applicable-with-rationale trigger matrix; a stronger architecture core and risk-triggered extensions; broader but bounded UX-plan triggers; a disposition table for security, privacy, data, reliability, operations, performance, migration, integration, content, accessibility, and validation showing whether each belongs in an existing companion, a new candidate companion, downstream Plan, or no change; explicit duplicate-owner and template-bloat kills; current-package delta proposals; validator and negative-fixture requirements; and prioritized change requests for Invoke Design. Separate authored completeness from validated readiness. No canonical mutation is authorized. Do not write files. Your synthesis will be challenged by three independent skeptics.

agents.angle: Precedent and owner-fit attack: verify that proposed additions reuse current Invoke, UX-plan, architecture, research, Distill, decision-gate, implementation-layering, and work-pack ownership before inventing a family. Schön predicts that Popper may reject useful qualitative risk triggers merely because an automated validator is not yet available, while Popper predicts that Schön may accept nominal precedent without a failing witness. Schön predicts that Tetlock may split terms more finely than implementation ownership needs, while Tetlock predicts that Schön may treat overlapping labels as equivalent contracts.
agents.initial_prompt: Review the synthesis as the precedent and owner-fit skeptic. Verify every proposed Design section, trigger, companion, and gate against the live owned templates and external precedents actually cited. Mark reuse, extend-owned, candidate-new-family, or reject. Find cargo-cult standards use, duplicate ownership, universal checklist bloat, public-private leakage, and proposals whose owner is absent. Precedent results guide ownership and never kill a genuinely novel attempt by themselves. Return concrete objections, severity, and bounded revision requests. Do not write files.

agents.angle: Non-vacuity attack: attempt to make each trigger, new section, validation claim, and not-applicable path pass while the known defect remains, requiring independent denominators and negative fixtures. Schön predicts that Popper may reject useful qualitative risk triggers merely because an automated validator is not yet available, while Popper predicts that Schön may accept nominal precedent without a failing witness. Popper predicts that Tetlock may obtain clean definitions that still cannot catch a defect, while Tetlock predicts that Popper may accept executable checks that collapse distinct UX, architecture, and readiness meanings.
agents.initial_prompt: Review the synthesis as the non-vacuity skeptic. Attempt to construct cases where the trigger matrix omits a known UX, architecture, authority, state, security, data, reliability, operations, migration, or evidence defect, and cases where it needlessly selects every companion. Test whether required sections have independent denominators, missing-input and fabricated-completion fixtures, earliest-detection evidence, and falsifiable acceptance. KILL any recommendation that only adds prose or authored status without changing detection. Return concrete objections, severity, and exact revision requests. Do not write files.

agents.angle: Definitional-soundness attack: test whether UX, architecture, quality attribute, operations, validation, readiness, companion, trigger, and not-applicable are distinct, observable, and assigned to one owner. Schön predicts that Tetlock may split terms more finely than implementation ownership needs, while Tetlock predicts that Schön may treat overlapping labels as equivalent contracts. Popper predicts that Tetlock may obtain clean definitions that still cannot catch a defect, while Tetlock predicts that Popper may accept executable checks that collapse distinct UX, architecture, and readiness meanings.
agents.initial_prompt: Review the synthesis as the definitional-soundness skeptic. Audit the proposed risk taxonomy, selection outcomes, companions, owner boundaries, evidence classes, and handoff states. Find overlapping terms, circular selection rules, unobservable triggers, architecture or UX scope collapse, Design-versus-Plan leakage, and authored-complete versus validator-ready confusion. Require a minimal vocabulary and deterministic decision order. KILL unresolved definitional collapse. Return concrete objections, severity, and exact revision requests. Do not write files.

groups.anti_bias: write only the converged, evidence-bound coverage model and keep candidate changes subordinate to lifecycle owners

agents.angle: Normalize the converged result into one private design-coverage finding with traceable triggers, owner boundaries, killed alternatives, and bounded package deltas.
